accepted.pun_explanation: Pawsey is a real surname over a real family yard and it says palsy; the initial in front of it is the one every such board carries, and the two together read without a clinical word being painted anywhere. Stretching, serial casting and bracing are one job here and nobody calls them anything. My brief makes that an automatic reject. Stating the counter-argument plainly so the call can be overridden knowingly: the corpus does ship exactly this morpheme-split device — CLOZA PINE MILL, DOPA MINE No.4, SARA TONIN CARPETS — and the spec's own R1 licenses 'one morpheme of the diagnosis hand-lettered on a PROP inside a world that IS the term's literal picture'. problems: The sign indexes the specimen, not the disease. CSF is the workup's object; the chapter is CNS infection with psychiatric sequelae. Retrieval runs backwards: a resident who remembers CLEAR SPRING FISHERIES recovers 'cerebrospinal fluid', and has to already be thinking about lumbar puncture to get from there to meningitis. Rule 1 asks the name to be a pun on the topic; this is a pun on the test.

C-S-F as three word-initials is the weakest legal form of ACRONYM_EMBED. The corpus precedents work for reasons this one lacks: OUSE AMATEUR ROWING SOCIETY spells OARS, which is both a real word and the method's own four-skill acronym; OCEAN DAILY CATCH and expreSS tRIps bury the letters inside words. CSF is not a word, not fisheries vocabulary, and sits on three initials so common that almost any three-word trade name yields some acronym. The letters are asserted, not hidden.

The chapter's named second half — psychiatric sequelae — gets one prop: a day book with a repeated entry. That is the aspect that makes this a psychiatry chapter rather than an infectious-disease one, and the venue has no home for the specific syndromes the chapter must cover (HSV encephalitis and the temporal lobe, neurosyphilis, HIV, autoimmune encephalitis). Fish off the feed cannot carry any of them.

The discrimination the chapter actually turns on — bacterial vs viral, i.e. the cell count and the differential — has no carrier. 'Counting frame and grading table with the day's tallies on a clip' is generic; the venue gives clear-vs-cloudy and pressure and protein/glucose, then stops exactly where the exam question is.
Population fails R3. A trout farm on a weekday morning has three or four staff. Twelve-plus figures all lowering clarity discs into raceways is not a mundane day at this place, it is a staged one.

Fourth water/fish venue in the course after 43 (wet fish shop), 63 (LURA'S BAIT & TACKLE) and 10 (OLD SCHOOL AQUARIUM). 'Trout farm' is not a synonym of any of them and 'farm' is the fifth farm (19, 83, 85, 89), so this is not a rule breach — but the fascia also reuses SPRING, already on two signs (98 SPRING NARCISSUS SHOW, 112 PIPER & DODD SPRINGS), which is exactly the dilution rule 4 exists to prevent.

Minor trade error: a Secchi-type clarity disc is pond and lake gear. A concrete raceway is shallow, fast and already clear; you read a raceway by looking into it, not by lowering a disc down a marked cord.
Author's own confidence is 'workable', and the record was already rejected once — the failure here is the derivation, not the dressing.
flagged.fix_hint: Route the fascia through the disease, not the specimen: a phonetic pun hiding MENINGES or ENCEPHAL- in ordinary trade words, on premises busy enough to hold 25 strangers. The trade needs, natively: three layered coverings, a stiff neck, a bright light people flinch from, and a queue. Then carry the CSF workup inside as props, because the best devices in this proposal are portable and should survive the move — the feed sack stamped with a protein figure and a sugar figure, and the identical sack torn open and emptied beside the one bad line, is the strongest single object in the batch and belongs wherever this chapter ends up. A fishery numbers its pegs, so loci get carriers whose real job is to bear digits: peg 22 on the near staging, peg 7 where the aerator pipework runs, peg 15 on both banks. The two waters are named on one post at the path fork, ANGEL POOL and WILLOW POOL, so the two syndromes ride on ordinary lake names; and because the same peg 15 exists on both waters and the day ticket is stamped with which one you are on, the venue's own geography is genomic imprinting — one deleted stretch, and which side it came from decides everything about the day. flagged.place: The night shift in the No. 4 spinning room of a cotton mill: one ring frame running the whole length of the room with its rows of spindles whirring, the creel of roving bobbins above it, the lineshaft and its belts under the ceiling, gas mantles down the alley, and the end window looking out over the mill gate.
flagged.activity: Everyone is minding the frames — walking the alley watching for a broken end, piecing the ends up between finger and thumb, sweeping the fly off the rails, and lifting the full cops off the spindles into a skip when the doffing call goes round.
flagged.anchor_structure: The ring frame — one continuous machine the length of the room, its ring rail rising and falling along a row of spindles, the roving creel above it and the lineshaft and belts overhead — running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and dividing the room into the doffing alley, the frame itself, the creel and gearing end, and the stair-and-hoist bay by the window.
flagged.pun_explanation: A mill's whole capacity is counted in spindles, so the fascia is an ordinary mill name and the second stage's named waveform at the same time, and the word sleep is nowhere on the board. The isomorphism is the machine's own motion rather than a metaphor laid over it: the ring rail rises and falls all night long and lays the cop down in visible layers, four or five builds to a doff, with the deepest part of the traverse coming early in the build and the run at the top of it getting longer towards the end — a night's architecture drawn as ordinary machinery a resident can redraw from memory. The frame whose driving belt has been thrown off its pulley while every spindle on it still whirrs at full speed is the paradoxical stage, drive cut to everything that moves and nothing else slowed at all. The overlooker's round comes every ninety minutes, which is the cycle at its real length. The light-and-clock system that the circadian disorders break is all standing furniture here: the mill clock over the door, the timekeeper's board with the shift hours painted on, the gas mantle turned right down over the far end of the alley, and the knocker-up's pole and cap hung inside the door with its list of streets and times. The humidifier duct in the ceiling with its damper half shut and two swollen bags of fly jammed in the throat of it is the obstructed airway and its adenotonsillar cause on one object; the shaft bearing that rattles, falls silent, and then bangs is the snore with the pause in the middle of it. The doffer who cannot stand still and shakes one leg out against the frame leg between skips is restless legs, and the ages down the alley, from the half-timer at the creel to the old sweeper at the far end, carry the lifespan without a word being written.
